scope: ADR-0085 P4-C1 Adapter/DSH fault-safe convergence. Reuses the committed P4-A/P4-B isolated four-boundary stack (Product API/Gateway -> authenticated Runtime Adapter judgment route -> real DSH child/runtime subprocess -> Backend/MCP admit+result seams) with a keyless scripted deterministic provider. It injects real process faults at the Adapter/DSH boundary (adapter process kill during an in-flight provider request; DSH runtime child kill inside a live adapter; a genuinely stuck provider; a normal long-running provider; a no-durable-progress result) and verifies the DURABLE convergence contract: an undecided model attempt is never automatically re-sent after a process restart; a late/duplicate/foreign result of an old attempt is isolated (exact replay) or rejected and never committed twice; no duplicate provider call, proposal, event, ResearchTask, artifact, experiment, backtest, approval, paper-account/order/position/fill is created; and the system reaches a contract-allowed, explainable pending (durable 'admitted' stage call) or 'needs_attention' state. The model never decides next_action, identity, approval, idempotency, routing or recovery state. P4-C1 does NOT claim DSH-native cross-process continuation or provider recovery, does NOT implement or claim P4-C2 (Backend claim/settle consumer) or P4-D (unified final verdict), and does not claim an overall P4 all_pass.
llm_evidence_note: A keyless deterministic fault-mode provider drives the real DSH child/runtime subprocess path. This is service-boundary/contract evidence, NOT real-LLM research-quality semantic evidence.

required_fault_rows.description: While a provider request is in flight, the Runtime Adapter OS process is really killed and restarted. The same undecided attempt is retried and is refused with an explicit in-progress (409) WITHOUT any new provider call, new stage call or business write; the durable stage call stays one 'admitted' row with call_index 1 and the plan/plan_version/iteration are unchanged.

The real DSH runtime child OS process is really killed INSIDE a live Runtime Adapter process. The bounded turn fails closed (503) and submits no result; the adapter pid is unchanged, the durable stage call stays 'admitted' and a retry of the same attempt is an explicit 409 in-progress with zero new provider calls.

After the adapter restart, repeated retries of the undecided attempt are each an explicit 409 in-progress with zero provider calls, no new stage call and no receipt; the pending attempt is never automatically re-sent.

After a legitimate judgment turn completes and advances the plan, a late request for the OLD attempt returns the stored receipt as an exact replay (model turn skipped) with zero provider calls, no new stage call and no plan/object change.

A late result submitted to the real Backend result seam for the OLD (already completed) call identity is an exact replay of the stored receipt and never a second write; a forged/foreign call identity is rejected; the plan and every business object count are unchanged.

A killed adapter owner and a genuinely stuck (still-live, provider blocked) owner produce the SAME undecided pending outcome: an explicit in-progress with a closed code and no fabricated receipt; the live/stale attempt is not auto-fenced to needs_attention and no recovery is claimed because the old owner's termination cannot be proved.

A genuinely running long turn (provider alive but delayed) completes once and advances the plan; a concurrent duplicate during the run is an explicit 409 in-progress and preempts nothing; the turn makes exactly its profile provider calls, exactly one stage call is completed and no duplicate business object is created. This distinguishes a normal long run from a killed/stuck owner.

A fresh bounded turn whose closed result carries no durable progress atomically moves the plan AND the ResearchTask to needs_attention with reason no_durable_progress in one transaction; exactly one stage call is completed with outcome needs_attention and no duplicate business object is created.

Across every fault scenario the observed object counts equal the expected counts: exactly one ResearchTask and one execution plan per scenario, one stage-call row per attempt, and no duplicate event/artifact/approval/job/backtest/paper account/order/position/fill.

required_boundary_rows.description: Real boundary controls over the authenticated adapter route: a missing service token, a forged token and a forged/stale attempt binding are all refused and reach neither the provider nor the durable stage-call ledger.
The isolated stack is torn down to zero containers/networks/volumes and the production compose project is never touched.

The adapter-derived call identity, the Backend stage-call identity and the receipt call identity are exactly equal; call_index is server-derived and exact; the plan CAS and generation state are consistent across the fault.

The adapter derives the call identity/attempt/read-only endpoint/DSH home server-side; a model result can never supply a next_action, identity, approval, idempotency key, routing or recovery state, and a non-'none' durable evidence identity fails closed.

Every observed terminal state after a fault is either an undecided durable 'admitted' pending or a structured needs_attention; there is no fabricated completed/recovered state and no state outside the closed plan/attempt vocabulary.

fault_injection_modes.adapter_process_kill: docker kill the isolated runtime-adapter container during an in-flight provider request
fault_injection_modes.dsh_child_kill: SIGKILL the real bundled DSH runtime child OS process inside the live runtime-adapter container
fault_injection_modes.provider_block_child: the keyless provider holds the child provider request open (a genuinely stuck owner)
fault_injection_modes.provider_delay_child: the keyless provider delays the child provider response (a normal long-running owner)
fault_injection_modes.provider_no_progress_child: the keyless provider returns a valid closed result with no durable progress

non_claims: P4-C1 verifies Adapter/DSH process-interruption convergence only; it does NOT claim DSH-native cross-process continuation or provider recovery.
P4-C1 does NOT implement or claim P4-C2 (Backend claim/settle real consumer) or P4-D (unified final verdict).
No overall P4 all_pass and no phase completion.
No production deployment, version write, tag or release.
No real-LLM research-quality semantic claim (keyless scripted provider).
No Phase 100 resume and no 0.10 start.
No second generic agent harness or session store.
